dedupe_keys.name: code and data for hierarchical multi agent reinforcement learning of emergency responder stationing nashville and seattle icml 2024

description: This package holds the code and data behind a method for deciding where to station ambulances and other emergency responders between calls, presented at the International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML) in 2024. It was deposited on figshare in May 2024 by Amutheezan Sivagnanam, Ava Pettet, Hunter Lee, Ayan Mukhopadhyay and Abhishek Dubey. The approach keeps the hierarchical spatial decomposition used by the best earlier method, which relies on online Monte Carlo tree search and can take minutes per decision, but replaces the search with reinforcement learning: actor-critic agents with transformers for variable-sized states and actions, projections to fixed-size observations and combinatorial mapping of continuous actions to discrete allocations. It is evaluated on real-world emergency data from Nashville, Tennessee and Seattle, Washington. The package, about 255 MB, is free to download under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: the metadata do not describe the file layout or how the city incident data were prepared, so users must read the package and paper. Simulation uses: incident streams, station sets and trained agents for testing ambulance repositioning and dispatch policies. Related records: the Seattle real-time fire 911 calls (data-seattle-real-time-fire-911-calls-p02674) are a public source of incidents in one of the two cities, and the Dutch proactive relocation pilot (case_study-netherlands-ambulance-dispatch-proactive-relocation-pilot) shows relocation in practice.
